transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love—my workshop, church, even fishing don’t mean anything to me right now. My wife and my pastor jointly encouraged me to come in because I've just completely withdrawn from everything. I just feel very weary and defeated.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you ever experienced similar periods of feeling like this in the past?

These feelings really took a strong hold about three weeks ago, shortly after my doctor raised concerns about my memory and restricted my driving. I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life—it is entirely new and seems tied to these recent health worries.
Along with feeling weary and losing interest in your hobbies, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or appetite over these past three weeks?

Food just doesn't appeal to me lately, and it feels like too much effort to fix a proper meal, so I often get by on just a cup of coffee and a piece of toast. As for my sleep, I haven't really noticed any major changes in my patterns.
Along with feeling defeated, have you been experiencing any feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts that life is no longer worth living?

I do feel completely useless now that my mind is so foggy and I can't handle basic things anymore. At night, when the house is quiet, I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn't wake up so my wife wouldn't have to watch me fall apart. I don't have any plans to harm myself, but those thoughts have definitely been creeping in.
Besides feeling weary and defeated, have you been feeling sad, down, or empty for most of the day, nearly every day over these past three weeks?

Yes, most days I feel this heavy, hollow ache in my chest, like someone turned the color down on everything. I keep catching myself thinking, "What’s the point of any of this now that I might just be fading away upstairs?" It has been happening nearly every day for the past three weeks, ever since my doctor brought up those memory issues.
Have you or your wife noticed if you are moving, speaking, or reacting much slower than usual, or on the other hand, if you feel unusually restless and unable to sit still?

My wife actually keeps asking if I’m sick because I’ve slowed down so much, shuffling around the house and taking forever just to get dressed. Sometimes I'll find myself just sitting at the kitchen table, staring blankly at the salt shaker for ten minutes before I even realize I haven't moved. I don't feel restless at all; everything just feels incredibly slow and heavy now.
Have you noticed any new difficulties with concentrating, making decisions, or focusing on simple daily tasks since this heavy mood started?

Yes, it's been incredibly difficult. As a former engineer who used to handle complex projects, it is very frustrating to now lose my train of thought mid-conversation or struggle with simple decisions like choosing which shirt to wear. Everything just blends together into this foggy, frustrating blur.
Do you find that this heavy, empty feeling is constantly there throughout the day, even when you aren't actively thinking about your memory or driving situation?

Yes, it really is constantly there, acting like a heavy background fog that never lifts. Even when I'm not actively worrying about my memory or driving, everything still feels completely dull and colorless. It's as if the volume and color of my life have just been permanently turned down.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt the exact opposite of this—unusually energetic, happy, or hyperactive for days at a time, perhaps needing very little sleep?
No, I've never had any periods where I felt unusually energetic or hyperactive like that. Before this recent cloud came over me, my mood was always very steady and even-keeled.
Did you notice any of these memory or concentration difficulties before your doctor brought them up, or did they only start around the same time as your low mood?

Actually, the memory and concentration issues started first, about six months after I retired, when I began misplacing my tools and even left the stove on. Those lapses are what led to the doctor's visit in the first place. The heavy mood and feeling of uselessness only set in about three weeks ago, after the doctor brought up the cognitive testing and restricted my driving.
Did your doctor diagnose you with a specific medical or neurological condition, such as a thyroid problem, a stroke, or a brain disease, to explain your memory issues?

No, there isn't a final diagnosis yet. My primary care doctor only raised concerns about "possible mild cognitive impairment" and ordered neurocognitive testing, but we are still waiting on the results. It's incredibly frustrating being in this limbo, especially since I've had to cut back on driving and my usual activities in the meantime.
Have you noticed any other physical or neurological symptoms recently, such as tremors, weakness on one side of your body, or trouble with your balance?

No, I haven't noticed any of those specific things like tremors, weakness on one side, or balance issues. I do feel generally slow and sluggish, as I mentioned before, but nothing like physical shaking or weakness.
Has anyone in your close family, such as your parents or siblings, ever struggled with or been treated for depression or other mood disorders?

I'm not aware of anyone in my immediate family ever struggling with depression or mood disorders. As far as I can recall, neither my parents nor my siblings ever had to be treated for anything like that.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, or has there been any recent change in your use of alcohol?

I do take a few daily medications, but my wife has had to remind me to take them lately and I can't quite recall their names right now. As for alcohol, I don't really drink, so there hasn't been any change in that regard.
Even though you can't recall the names of your medications, do you know what specific medical conditions you are taking them for, such as high blood pressure, thyroid issues, or heart problems?
To be honest, I'm not really sure what they are for anymore. My mind has been so foggy lately that my wife handles all of my pills, and I just take whatever she gives me.
Have you had any brain scans, like an MRI or a CT scan, as part of the medical evaluation for your memory issues?
No, I haven't had any brain scans like an MRI or a CT scan yet. So far, my primary care doctor has only ordered the neurocognitive testing, and we are still waiting on those results.
Do you have a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or any heart conditions?
No, I don't have a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or any heart conditions. My doctor has never mentioned any of those issues to me.
Have you recently had any blood tests done, and if so, did your doctor mention any abnormal results, such as with your thyroid or vitamin levels?
I don't recall having any recent blood tests done for my thyroid or vitamins. My doctor only mentioned ordering the neurocognitive testing, so I'm really not sure about any blood work.
